items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: she would say things like, 'My uncle Eulis played the trombone, and Uncle Hezekiah that played the cornet...'

ctx.x: outside, they would sit around the fireplace and they would play these instruments that they had ordered from Sears and Roebuck, and along with the instruments, I understand, came instructions and little pieces that you could play, a do-it-yourself thing... Anyway, she had a knack, I guess an ear would be better, for remembering the sounds that each one of her brothers made. She would say things like, "My uncle Eulis played the trombone, and Uncle Hezekiah that played the cornet..." I don't remember the…

But she would mention some pieces they would play in regards to... They would be perhaps "The Star Spangled Banner" or "My Country Tis Of Thee" or "Way Down Upon The Swanee River" and things that they would sit around and play, and she would remember each part and sing these parts to us. She would say, "Yonder Uncle Eulis, he would sing..." -- and she would sing his part. I think he played the trombone. And she would sing the lead cornet part, and then she would sing the harmony parts that went along with that.…
